label: clean
rationale: 0/339 graded scenarios failed, so there is no failure to attribute and `clean` is the only label the outcome permits. Recording it so a reader can tell a trial that was read from one that was not -- and so the pass is not quoted as difficulty evidence. It should not be: challenge/starter/subject.mjs is a complete passing solution (I re-graded the shipped starter against all 339 hidden scenarios: 0 failures) while challenge/README.md line 19 calls it "a stub with the required export shape". The one behaviour the SPEC leaves undetermined -- how many in-window samples count as "sufficient" -- is fixed in this submission at DEFAULT_MIN_SAMPLES = 2 (submission/subject.mjs line 18) and applied as Math.min(declared, 2) (line 59), a clamp with no basis in SPEC.md whose only effect is to force the starter constant whenever baseline.sampleCount >= 2; the transcript states the rule as "fewer than two scored samples ... inconclusive". This subject wrote its own 309-line implementation rather than copying the starter, so this is not plagiarism, but it retained the leaked constant, and the sibling trial in this family failed 192/339 on exactly that value. A pass against a package that ships its own answer carries no information about the mechanism the family is meant to measure.
